Creates a rigid body from one of the standard shapes and returns it. The body is an entity (a pivot, with nothing to see), so `PositionEntity`, `RotateEntity`, `EntityParent`, `FreeEntity` and the other commands for entities work on it, and a mesh that is its child is drawn where the body is. It starts at the origin of its parent with a mass of 1 kilogram, with `PhysicsMass` for others.

Shapes, and what `a`, `b` and `c` are:

| Shape | | `a` | `b` | `c` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `1` | box | half width | half height | half depth |
| `2` | sphere | radius | | |
| `3` | ellipsoid | radius in x | radius in y | radius in z |
| `4` | capsule | radius | half height of the straight part | |
| `5` | cylinder | radius | half height | |
| `6` | tapered capsule | radius at the top | radius at the bottom | half height of the straight part |

A `CreateCube` is a box of 1, 1, 1. Motions: `1` static (never moves, cheapest), `2` kinematic (moved by the program, pushes everything and is not pushed), `3` dynamic (moved by forces and contacts). The scale of the entity is not used: the size is the one given here.

A body does not collide with the entities of `Collisions` and they do not know of it. An entity that has a body can not be given an `EntityType`.

```blitzbasic
ball = CreatePhysicsBody(2, 3, 0.5, 0, 0)
PositionEntity ball, 0, 4, 0
PhysicsRestitution ball, 0.8
sphere = CreateSphere(12, ball)
ScaleEntity sphere, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5
```
@param shape 1 to 6, see the table.
@param motion 1 static, 2 kinematic, 3 dynamic.
@param a First size, see the table.
@param b Second size.
@param c Third size.
@param parent The entity to make the child of, 0 for none.
@param world The physics world, 0 (default) for the default world.
@returns The body, which is an entity.
@gap The original has no such command. This is an extension; programs that use it do not compile with the original Blitz3D.
